messages.author: 592c5a3dc900f9f9
messages.subject: spPGOcc Error
parts:
Hello,

Thank you for creating these packages and setting up this platform for questions. I have a query regarding spOccupancy.

I am attempting to do a nationwide occupancy assessment of a rare species. I have camera trap data from ~1500 camera traps from nine sites across Uganda, therefore the survey design is clustered with distance between all cameras ranging from <20m to >500,000km. The detection history is up to 36 5-day sampling occasions (~6 months) for each camera.

To fully explore my data, and as this is my first time using the package (and Bayesian stats!), I have done a number of exploratory steps to help my understanding. Firstly, I ran occupancy models using unmarked to see whether the models would converge with all my variables and explore which variables were most influential. I then ran the  ‘PGOcc’ function on the null, global and best resulting model from unmarked – these all ran without any issues using the defaults from the article here: Introduction to spOccupancy • spOccupancy

However, the reason for wanting to use this package was to explore and account for any issues with spatial correlation.  I used the ‘spPGOcc’ function on the full dataset (not taking into account the clustered sample design) on the null, global and best models, again using the default values from the blog above. The models ran but my rhat values were incredibly large. For example, here is the summary output from my global model:


 

After reading this blog,

Convergence diagnostics and other considerations when fitting spatial occupancy models • spOccupancy

 and the paper by Bajcz et al. (2024) I have tried to use more informed priors, using minimum and maximum distances between cameras within each study site rather than the whole country, which ranges from ~ 20m – 40km. I used the equation in Bajcz et al to calculate X and W, but have left all other remaining values the same, as so:

informed.priors <- list(beta.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72),

                    alpha.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72),

                    sigma.sq.ig = c(2, 1),

                    phi.unif = c(3/(40754/2), 1/1903))

However, when I try to run any models, they fail to run, and I get the following error message:

Error in spPGOcc(occ.formula = null.formula, det.formula = null.formula,  : c++ error: dpotrf failed

I have checked for duplicated coordinates but there aren’t any. Does anyone have any suggestions on what might be going wrong?


Any guidance would be greatly appreciated.

 

Best wishes,

Naomi

messages.author: 2fac80955b0c9c31
messages.subject: Re: spPGOcc Error
parts:
Hi Naomi, 

In the past I had the same error and it was all about the coordinates. See here for a reply from Jeff.
In my case the problem were some few duplicates that were difficult to detect, but I see that you checked that already! So maybe make sure that you have projected coordinate system and not WGS84 with lat-long or put a more informative prior (see the response of Jeff for more info). 

Hope it helps,

Juan

messages.author: 0b274a0ee3490d75
messages.subject: Re: spPGOcc Error
parts:
Hi Naomi, 

My first guess as to why you're getting that error is because you may have an invalid initial value for phi. If you were using the initial values described in the vignette and did not change the initial value for phi after specifying a more informative prior, then it is likely outside the range of the uniform prior that is specified on phi and will result in an immediate error like the one you have there. You could either specify the initial value for phi to make sure it is within the bounds of the new uniform distribution you are specifying in "phi.unif", or you could just take the initial value for phi out of the "spat.inits" list completely, in which case the function will by default choose a good initial value for you. Once you do that I'm guessing the error should go away. 

Additionally, I noticed you are running the model for 10,000 samples per chain, which is not all that much for a spatial occupancy model, particularly when you have a lot of sites. While 10,000 iterations in the vignette resulted in a model that converged (or was very close to converging), that may not be the case for other data sets, particularly one like yours where you have substantially more sites than what I used in the vignette. So, you may need to run the model for 50,000 iterations or even 100,000 iterations (or potentially more). 

Let me know if I can clarify anything,

Jeff

messages.author: 0b274a0ee3490d75
messages.subject: Re: spPGOcc Error
parts:
Hi Naomi,

Gerat, glad to hear that you've got the models to run. Yes, you should try and ensure that phi is converged and less than 1.1 as well, although this (and sigma.sq) are notoriously difficult parameters to get to converge so it may be more difficult to achieve than for the other parameters. First, I would suggest looking at the traceplots for the spatial covariance parameters, which you can do with plot(out, 'theta', density = FALSE), where you replace the name of "out" with whatever you saved your output from spPGOcc as. This will give you more of an indication of the convergence of phi as opposed to just the Rhat value. You also will likely want to increase the burn-in to something larger than 2000, perhaps to something like 40,000. That may remove some parts of the sample towards the beginning of the model run that have not reached convergence (which you may see in the traceplot).

Jeff
